prompt: Why start a self-review from the diff rather than the files in the editor?

choices.text: It shows exactly what you changed, which is what a reviewer reads first
The editor hides the comments that a reviewer needs to see
The diff runs the tests on each file before showing it to you
Editors cannot open the JavaScript files of a project

prompt: What does main...empty-state mean in git diff?

choices.text: Every difference between the two tips, both ways
choices.why: That is closer to two dots.

choices.text: The commits on main that the branch does not have yet
What the branch changed since it left main, and nothing else
A range covering the last three commits on the branch

prompt: How many lines did the empty-state change add, by the stat?
What does the lesson say about a diff you cannot read in one sitting?

choices.text: Nobody will read it carefully, and that includes you
It shows ambition, which is what reviewers reward in a junior
It is fine as long as every test still passes
It should be merged without review, to save time

prompt: What did the grep over the added lines find? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A console.log in app.js
A TODO comment in index.html
The borrower's name drawn as markup
A debugger statement
choices.why: The pattern looked for one; there was none.

prompt: Why does the grep pattern start with ^\+?

choices.text: It matches only lines with a plus sign in the code
It looks only at lines the branch adds
It makes grep ignore the difference between upper and lower case
It counts the matching lines instead of printing them

prompt: Which problem in the change's surroundings did reading find and no grep could?

choices.text: A borrower's name put into the page as HTML
A TODO left in a comment
A console.log in load()
A missing semicolon at the end of a line in app.js

prompt: Match each checklist question to what it catches.

pairs.left: Does every name say what the thing is?

pairs.right: An old version kept just in case

pairs.left: Would I understand this in six months?
pairs.right: A clever line with no comment

prompt: Why does commented-out code not belong in a change, by the table?

choices.text: Git already keeps every old version in the history
Comments slow the program down when the browser loads it
Linters refuse to run on a file that contains it
It is a security hole in itself, whatever it contains

prompt: Where are the slips found in self-review fixed?

choices.text: In a later pull request, once this one is merged
On the same branch, folded into the commit it fixes
Nowhere, since neither of them breaks anything that runs
Directly on main, after the branch has been merged

prompt: After the fixup, what count did grep -c report?
Where does the lesson fix the injection problem, and why?

choices.text: In this pull request, since it was found here
Nowhere; it is not a real problem
choices.why: It was fixed in lesson 13's commit.

choices.text: In the README, listed as a known issue for readers
choices.why: It is fixed, not only noted.

choices.text: In its own change with its own card, since it predates this one

prompt: Which are the lesson's tests that a self-review is finished? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: You would be comfortable seeing the diff pinned to a wall with your name
You can say in one sentence what the change does
The diff is longer than a hundred lines
Somebody else has approved it

prompt: Put the parts of the description in the example's order.
Which part do people skip and reviewers value most?

choices.text: What
Why
The title
How I checked

prompt: What goes in "not in this change"?

choices.text: A list of every file in the repository the change did not touch
The features cut from the project, with their reasons
A problem found in review, with its card
An apology for how long the change took to finish

prompt: Why open a pull request you will merge yourself?

choices.text: Git refuses to merge any branch that has no pull request
It runs the checks and leaves the description for the next reader
It hides the branch's commits from git log once merged
It sends the change to a random reviewer on the site

prompt: Which ways of getting distance does the lesson give? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Read it the next morning
Read it in the pull-request page instead of the editor
Read the tests first
Read it as fast as possible

prompt: What does a line you cannot explain out loud tell you, by the lesson?

choices.text: It is too short to matter to anybody reading the project
The interviewer in lesson 20 will ask you about it
It should be deleted at once and written again from scratch
It needs more lines of comment than lines of code

prompt: A pull request adds a route, its test, a print('here') and a rename of an unrelated function. What does self-review do?
hint: A slip and a second idea.

choices.text: Keep all of it, since every test passes and the route works
Remove the test, since the print shows it works
Remove the print, and move the rename to its own change
Merge it now, and clean it all up in a later pull request

prompt: A description says only "fixed stuff". Which part would help a reviewer most, by the lesson?

choices.text: A longer title that lists every file the change touched
A list of every commit hash in the branch, oldest first
An apology for the size of the change
How I checked: what was run, and what was not tested and why
